interpretation: A single paired pilot is not a population comparison. Online controller stretches can begin in different states; frozen trials use the same initial state and duration, with no Astra calls.

turns.note: Initially upright with left support. Test a modest alternating joint-feedback oscillator with torso damping.
Run briefly to measure balance, joint response, and contact changes.
Large torques caused immediate backward rotation and saturation. Reduce gains sharply and reverse torso feedback to oppose measured rotation.
Restart upright to test reduced-gain feedback independently of the fall.
Measure low-gain balance and alternating clearance over half a cycle.
Reduced gains avoid immediate instability, but both feet remain planted. Observe whether the next cycle produces separation or drift.
Both feet stayed planted while ankles yielded and the body fell forward. Increase leg support and alternating flexion, with forward torso bias and speed-dependent ankle braking.
Reset for the stronger support controller.
Test stronger knee and ankle support for one full oscillator cycle.
Upright at one second, but no foot clearance. Increase alternating knee flexion and hip excursion while retaining support gains.
Test larger alternating flexion from the current upright state.
Two seconds upright but zero touchdowns; feet remain anchored. Test substantially deeper alternating knee flexion to force clearance, with stronger ankle braking.
Reset before testing deep flexion; current body is already tipping forward.
Check whether deep flexion produces an actual supported swing.
Deep flexion cleared the right foot but carried it backward. Reverse hip phase and shift torso equilibrium forward to test forward placement.
Test revised hip phasing from the standard initial pose.
Observe forward-biased alternating flexion over one cycle.
Both feet now show swing intervals but no qualifying forward landing yet. Continue to measure whether forward momentum produces steps.
Swing occurs but feet do not land forward before collapse. Shift hip phase toward late-swing extension, moderate knee flexion, and increase speed braking.
Restart for the phase-shifted, speed-braked controller.
Test late-swing placement and stronger speed feedback for two seconds.
Positive ankle speed feedback amplified backward motion. Reverse that feedback while retaining the phase-shifted swing.
Reset to test reversed ankle speed feedback.
Measure stability and touchdown direction with negative speed feedback.
One alternating count was recorded, but forward speed and height diverged. Test a backward torso equilibrium for foot reach and gentler ankle speed feedback.
Restart to evaluate the revised torso and ankle balance.
Test revised balance for two seconds, checking qualifying landings rather than distance alone.
A supported forward landing occurred at 0.5 s, followed by ankle yielding and collapse. Keep that swing pattern but restore strong ankle position support.
Restart for the ankle-support contrast.
Check whether stronger ankle support permits repeated alternating landings.
Strong ankle support reversed the failure into backward collapse. Test intermediate ankle stiffness and torso bias, retaining the swing phase that produced a forward landing.
Reset for the intermediate-gain test.
Evaluate intermediate balance gains over three seconds or until a fall.

Walking was not demonstrated. Latest attempt reached 1.013 m but fell at 2.10 s with zero qualifying steps. Earlier attempts recorded at most one alternating step; balance and repeated forward placement remain unresolved.
Initially upright with left-foot support. A brief right-leg flexion probe tests joint direction and foot clearance while the left leg supports the body.
The open-loop probe produced rapid backward torso rotation, so reset before testing closed-loop joint and torso feedback.
Test a damped near-standing controller first; joint feedback should prevent the uncontrolled rotation seen in the probe.
Run briefly to measure whether joint damping and pitch feedback stabilize the initial stance.
The feedback oscillated within two ticks and saturated. Reduce stiffness and damping substantially to test numerical stability.
Reset the fallen body to test the reduced-gain controller from the same initial pose.
Measure reduced-gain stance stability over 0.6 seconds.
Reduced gains kept the torso upright for 0.6 seconds, but both feet stayed grounded. Add alternating hip motion and knee flexion to test foot clearance and forward touchdowns.
Test whether alternating flexion lifts the feet while preserving torso balance.

Motion advanced the body but produced no qualifying steps; both feet remained behind it. Test a crouched alternating gait with ankle targets compensating leg angles and stronger forward-speed braking.
Reset to evaluate the crouched gait without the previous forward fall momentum.
Test the revised gait for one second, checking actual lift-off and touchdown rather than body displacement alone.
The ankle compensation drove a backward fall; its knee sign was incorrect. Correct the foot-angle compensation and use a modest backward torso lean with alternating knee clearance.
Restart for the corrected ankle-compensation test.
Measure the corrected controller's balance and alternating contacts over one second.
Forward speed grew to 2.12 m/s with no valid steps. Reverse the ankle speed correction to brake that growth, and deepen the backward lean needed to place bent legs beneath the torso.
Reset before testing speed braking and the revised torso lean.
Test whether reversed ankle feedback contains speed and enables repeated lift-offs.
Repeated runs leave both feet behind the body and lose height. Replace ankle angle tracking with support-foot position/velocity feedback and separate stance torso control from swing-leg positioning.
Reset to test the separated stance and swing controller.
Check whether stance feedback holds the torso while the opposite leg swings forward.
The new controller stayed upright and produced one verified right touchdown. Continue unchanged to assess repeated alternating steps and net travel.
Balance now lasts 3.2 seconds, but only right touchdowns qualify. Apply foot-leveling only to the swinging ankle and retain support feedback on the stance ankle, with slightly more forward drive.
Test swing-foot leveling and greater clearance for alternating left and right touchdowns.
Walking demonstrated: 1.235 m forward, five alternating qualifying touchdowns, upright at 5.2 s, and current speed 0.526 m/s. Simulator reports success.
